researchNotes.title: Hoid’s Sixth Word
researchNotes.description: Hoid describes a sense telling him when important events will occur and says he obtained the Words from a place whose story he has not told. The exact origin and mechanics remain undisclosed; calling the Sixth Word a Dawnshard or assigning a Shard would go beyond this passage.

researchNotes.title: The unidentified dragon
researchNotes.description: Hoid explicitly distinguishes the dragon who helped the Prophet from both the Prophet and Valor. It is unnamed and requested removal from the stories. No particular dragon identity is confirmed.
researchNotes.locator: Fires XXVI, correction to the tour guide’s legend.

researchNotes.title: Jasper and the Tzendish cult
researchNotes.description: Hoid mentions influencing religion on Jasper and separately recalls joining a Tzendish cult. Neither aside identifies another published story as its source, so these remain unpaired references rather than invented book links.

researchNotes.title: Shattering-related asides
researchNotes.description: Hoid says he helped kill God, then later jokes about helping cause the collapse of reality. The first statement is explicit; identifying the later joke as a specific additional event would be an interpretation. It is not evidence for a second Shattering.

researchNotes.title: The final bond is unusual
researchNotes.description: December’s final sharing of her soul with the negative-power entity goes beyond simple command and obedience, and Hoid says scholars have not replicated it. Treating this exceptional outcome as a standard example of every Zuhel bond would overstate the text.
researchNotes.locator: Fires XXXIV (first bond), XXXVII (release) and XLII (final bond).

researchNotes.title: Valor’s trap and three dragon-ruled worlds
researchNotes.description: The epilogue reveals that Valor’s temple burns Hoid again and that its murals prompt him to seek three worlds ruled by dragons. The worlds are not named. This does not establish they are Yolen, any particular future book setting, or all one known system.

researchNotes.title: Why the Cosmere name is “December”
researchNotes.description: Hoid says he is translating the name; the local form is Hodołnika. In the postscript, Sanderson explains that December is his own birth month and that he chose it for its end-of-one-life/beginning-of-another associations. This is a translation convention and an authorial naming detail, not evidence that Miral uses Earth’s calendar.
researchNotes.locator: Fires I, narrator’s translation and the local name; Postscript, naming explanation.

audit.method: Systematic full-text search with contextual candidate verification
audit.limitations: Not a line-by-line literary reread or an exhaustive illustration/annotation audit. Wind and Truth is not fully audited. Exact unnamed identities and chronology remain unresolved.

connections.title: The Prophet and Nalthian power
connections.description: Separate findings and their evidence are listed below. Arrow direction indicates background context, not a required reading sequence.
connections.locator: See the locator for each individual finding.

claims.title: The Prophet is Vasher
claims.description: Sanderson confirms the identity. He corrects the historical visit to before Warbreaker, during Vasher’s travels involving Roshar and Sel. This dates the Prophet’s earlier visit, not December’s main story.
claims.locator: FanX 2026, September 25, entry 3; Fires XLI and Epilogue corroborate the character’s later activities.

claims.title: Breaths, passphrases and purified power
claims.description: Hoid first proposes repurposed Breaths, then explains a buffer of transformed Breath-adjacent Investiture between the Aon and silver. Its power has been purified of its original Intent. He describes transfer, withdrawal and dispersal passphrases; these are not ordinary unmodified Breaths or a complete recipe for conventional Awakening.
claims.locator: Fires XXVII (initial hypothesis); XXXVIII (Hoid’s explanation); Epilogue (passphrase changes).

claims.title: T’Telir’s Court of Gods
claims.description: Hoid explicitly compares Kingseat’s colors with T’Telir’s Court of Gods, the Warbreaker setting. This is a named place reference; it does not identify Hoid’s audience as Nalthian.
claims.locator: Fires IX, description of Kingseat’s fashion.

claims.title: A Nalthian audience?
claims.description: The colorful-clothing comparison has prompted a Nalthian or Hallandren audience theory. That audience identification is not established here.
claims.locator: Fires IX. Audience identification is not stated; the Court of Gods comparison alone does not identify the listeners.

claims.title: The Prophet’s dream and emissary
claims.description: December encounters the Prophet through the Spiritual Realm. In the epilogue he sends a simulacrum that he directs remotely because he cannot leave Roshar. The historical demon-binding visit and this later interaction are different events. The Vasher identification still relies on the separate author confirmation.
claims.locator: Fires XLI, December’s dream; Epilogue, the Prophet’s visit.

claims.title: Returned terminology, without a Returned cameo
claims.description: While explaining his disembodied state, Hoid explicitly says he is not a Cognitive Shadow, Returned, Herald or Creed Wraith. Returned is familiar Warbreaker terminology, but the passage does not turn Hoid into a Returned or add an unnamed Returned appearance.
claims.locator: Fires XXVII, opening explanation.

visual.label: The Prophet and Nalthian power
visual.credit: Original explanatory diagram; not official artwork.

claims.title: An Aon in a combined magical binding
claims.description: The prose names an Aon attached to the silver spike. Hoid later explains the intervening buffer of transformed power. An Aon is explicit in the text; the name Reo is not.
claims.locator: Fires XXVI (rune); XXVII (named Aon); XXXVIII (buffer).

claims.title: Aon on the Ever-Slaying Sword
claims.description: The binding incorporates an Aon. Coppermind identifies Reo in Tran Nguyen’s illustration; the exact Aon is not named in the prose. This is an illustration-specific identification.
claims.locator: Fires XXVI, Tran Nguyen’s “Less a Sword, More a Spike” illustration. Painting inspected; Reo identification retained from Coppermind, not named in prose.

claims.title: Rivers and purified Dor: comparison
claims.description: Purified power invites comparison with Dor, but the text does not identify Miral’s river as Selish Dor. The river is explained as matter released from the Megalith’s body. Do not conflate that river with the spike’s purified-power buffer.
claims.locator: Fires XXXVIII describes purified power in the spike’s buffer. The river’s identity as Dor is not established.

connections.title: Spiritweb pinning and Scadrial
connections.description: Separate findings and their evidence are listed below. Arrow direction indicates background context, not a required reading sequence.
connections.locator: See the locator for each individual finding.

claims.title: Hemalurgy-adjacent binding
claims.description: The Prophet targets a Hemalurgic bind point with a silver spike. Hoid calls the construction Hemalurgy-adjacent: it pins the entity rather than serving as an ordinary power-stealing spike. The Aon and transformed-power buffer explain why the soul cannot simply escape around the silver.
claims.locator: Fires XXVI (Hemalurgic bind point); XXVII (“Hemalurgy-adjacent”); XXXVIII (silver and buffer).

claims.title: A Scadrian second skin
claims.description: Hoid explicitly compares the responsive dress with a similar garment on Scadrial, after an aside about a literal and figurative second skin. This confirms the world reference, while the particular Scadrian garment and technology remain unidentified.
claims.locator: Fires XXIV, December’s demonblood gown.

claims.title: Scadrial’s old canals
claims.description: Hoid compares oxen towing Miral’s upriver barges with the old canals of Scadrial. This is an explicit historical/world reference, not a shared boat or a traveler cameo.
claims.locator: Fires III, the Northern Eclipse’s propulsion.

excerpt.locator: Fires III, the Northern Eclipse’s propulsion.

claims.title: A Soothing-like effect
claims.description: Hoid describes bathing in the demon’s blood as having a Soothing-like effect on emotions. He attributes it to the bound entity’s residual nature; the comparison does not establish that December is using brass Allomancy.
claims.locator: Fires XXIV, bathing and emotional dampening.

Its relationship to Threnody’s Evil is supplied by the reference and the wider entity lore in Emberdark. The novel does not name the Megalith as a shade or identify it as one particular Threnodite being.

claims.description: Compare the binding’s silver with its established effects on shades. The parallel is meaningful, but it does not establish that silver universally cancels all Investiture.

The shared lore does not make the Megalith, the encountered Threnodite entity and the Dakwara the same individual.

claims.title: Valor beyond a Shard-name mention
claims.description: Rhythm of War’s epigraph names Valor. Fires describes her work establishing religion on Miral, Hoid’s search for her, and the temple trap revealed in the epilogue. Medelantorius is not named in the uploaded Fires text; any vessel-name claim needs a separate source.

claims.title: Which memory incident?
claims.description: Hoid says he has memory backups because of earlier incidents, with an open-ended sequence of asides. Rhythm of War’s memory interference is a plausible referent, but Fires neither names the incidents nor limits them to exactly two.

connections.description: Separate findings and their evidence are listed below. Arrow direction indicates background context, not a required reading sequence.

claims.title: An explicit Ashyn reference
claims.description: Hoid thinks the fire used against him is Godsflame and explicitly says he thought it could not leave Ashyn. The epilogue locates his repeated burning in Valor’s temple trap. This supports an Ashyn link, while the material’s precise origin, mechanism and role in Ashyn’s catastrophe remain unproved.
claims.locator: Fires XXVII, Hoid’s Godsflame remark; Epilogue, the trap in Valor’s temple.

excerpt.text: I thought that stuff couldn’t leave Ashyn.
excerpt.locator: Fires XXVII, Hoid’s Godsflame remark; Epilogue, the trap in Valor’s temple.

claims.title: Another proposed memory incident
claims.description: Wind and Truth’s attack on Hoid is a proposed referent for his earlier-incident aside. The book does not identify an exact numbered incident; keep the assignment separate from the explicitly verified references.
claims.locator: Fires XXVII; proposed Wind and Truth incident in external discussion.

claims.title: Roshar and the Prophet’s confinement
claims.description: The Prophet’s dream describes a damaged land and an inability to leave. The epilogue explicitly identifies his current planet as Roshar and says he sends a simulacrum instead. A specific date relative to Wind and Truth is not stated in this passage.
claims.locator: Fires XLI and Epilogue.

claims.title: Silver across two systems
claims.description: The uploaded texts verify silver’s effects in both systems: Tress explains that it kills spores, while Fires explains its danger to the demon and the extra measures needed to pin its soul. These different effects are a comparison, not a universal rule that silver cancels all magic.
claims.locator: Fires XXVI and XXXVIII; Tress I (salt and silver), VIII “The Stowaway”, XXXI “The Midnight Essence”.

claims.title: Zuhel and Luhel
claims.description: Zuhel is named in Fires, and Tress explicitly explains Luhel and contrasts it with Nahel. The broader one-bond-per-Realm arrangement remains an interpretation, rather than a universal rule established by those passages.
claims.locator: Fires XXVII (Zuhel named), XXXIV, XXXVII and XLII (bond behavior); Tress XXXI “The Midnight Essence” (Luhel and Nahel contrasted).

claims.title: The Dougs return
claims.description: Fires calls the two sailors guarding December’s barge Doug and Doug, repeating Hoid’s shorthand for background characters explained in Tress. This is a narrator joke, not evidence that the sailors are the same people as the Crow’s Song crew.
claims.locator: Fires VII; Tress XIV “The Dougs”.

claims.title: Herald terminology, without a Herald cameo
claims.description: Hoid includes Herald among the labels he explicitly denies for his current condition. This is a Stormlight vocabulary reference, not evidence that a Herald appears on Miral or that every type of Cognitive Shadow works identically.
claims.locator: Fires XXVII, opening explanation.

claims.title: A cross-system bond comparison
claims.description: Zuhel bonds invite comparison with Stormlight’s Nahel bonds. The one-bond-per-Realm model remains a fan interpretation, and no identical cost or mechanism is asserted.
claims.locator: Fires XXVII and XLII; Tress XXXI explicitly contrasts Nahel and Luhel. A universal three-Realm model is not established.

claims.title: Design is away on a quest
claims.description: Hoid names Design and says she is away on a quest when he worries about his clothing. Yumi identifies Design as his Cryptic companion. This is a mention in Fires, not an on-page appearance, and her quest is not explained.
claims.locator: Fires XXXVIII; Yumi V (Design at the noodle shop) and “Another Epilogue”.

excerpt.text: If Design gets back from her quest
excerpt.locator: Fires XXXVIII; Yumi V (Design at the noodle shop) and “Another Epilogue”.

claims.title: A possible memory-protection parallel
claims.description: Yumi explicitly connects Hoid’s freezing with protection protocols adopted after his memories were stolen. Fires mentions backups and earlier incidents without naming them. Yumi supplies a relevant parallel, but it does not prove which incident any particular aside in Fires means.
claims.locator: Fires XXVII; Yumi “Another Epilogue”, Hoid’s explanation of his protection protocols.

claims.title: A magitech comparison
claims.description: Both texts use soul-related power in material form: Fires mines demonstone for cannonades; The Sunlit Man explains sunhearts. Similar function does not prove identical origin, manufacture or magical mechanics.
claims.locator: Fires XXVI (demonstone mining and cannonades); Sunlit Man XII (sunheart explanation). Comparison is interpretive.

claims.title: A planet where sunrise is too much
claims.description: Hoid alludes to a planet where sunrise can be excessive. Canticle’s lethal sunrise in The Sunlit Man is a strong candidate, but Fires does not name Canticle, so the identification remains an interpretation.
claims.locator: Fires XXXVIII, immediately before the conversation with Hoid; Sunlit Man I–II.

claims.description: The Silence Divine is a planned Ashyn story; Fires explicitly references Ashyn via Godsflame. This is a world-lore link, not evidence of a shared plot or a requirement to read an unpublished work.

claims.title: Staring down Ironeyes
claims.description: Hoid says December has stared Ironeyes straight on. This repeats the Mistborn death epithet; the sentence does not put Marsh physically on Miral. The connection is a linguistic allusion, not a cameo.
claims.locator: Fires VII, December’s response to a knife threat.
